edbDesc: An optical and electrical phenomenon in which a material becomes more electrically conductive due to the absorption of electromagnetic radiation such as visible light, ultraviolet light, infrared light, or gamma radiation.
title: Photoconductivity
description: Some materials, like selenium, let electricity through far more easily in light than in the dark. Willoughby Smith noticed in 1873 that the selenium resistors he used to test undersea telegraph cables gave readings that changed with the sunlight. Light meters, dusk-to-dawn streetlight switches, early TV cameras and the drum in every photocopier and laser printer use it.
effect: a material conducts electricity much better when light falls on it
usedIn: Photoconductive drums in photocopiers and laser printers
Cadmium sulfide sensors that switch streetlights on at dusk
strength: A cheap cadmium sulfide cell drops from millions of ohms in darkness to a few hundred ohms in daylight, a thousandfold change.
